overlap_rationale: Three independently trained skills match the three demonstrated physical relocations: red-to-buffer, blue-to-goal, and buffered-red-to-goal. No actions are excluded; every action is covered by at least one skill. S1→S2 shared supervised actions are demo10100[260,480)=220 (11.0 s), demo10101[270,480)=210 (10.5 s), demo10102[260,480)=220 (11.0 s), demo10103[260,480)=220 (11.0 s), demo10104[260,480)=220 (11.0 s), demo10105[250,480)=230 (11.5 s), demo10106[260,480)=220 (11.0 s), demo10107[260,490)=230 (11.5 s), and demo10108/10109/10110/10111[260,480)=220 each (11.0 s): 2,650 shared actions, 132.5 s total. This region includes red lowering/release and retreat, blue approach/contact/closure, and initial blue lift. S2→S3 shared supervised actions are demo10100[620,860)=240 (12.0 s), demo10101/10102/10103[620,850)=230 each (11.5 s), demo10104/10105[610,850)=240 each (12.0 s), demo10106[620,850)=230 (11.5 s), demo10107[630,860)=230 (11.5 s), and demo10108/10109/10110/10111[620,850)=230 each (11.5 s): 2,790 shared actions, 139.5 s total. This region includes blue lowering/release and retreat, buffered-red approach/contact/closure, and initial red lift. Boundary observations and front images establish scene context; only actions inside the listed half-open intervals are supervision. The expected benefit is robustness to switch timing and intermediate entry states, not proven recovery from unseen execution errors.
